Public blog revision · 11 September 2026

The revision preserves all 50 lessons and their source anchors. Each opening now states the mechanism directly. Repeated editorial purpose statements were removed while their attached definitions were retained. The landing page follows the argument from Fourier sampling through arithmetic to the machine schedule.

Mathematical comparisons are escaped before HTML parsing, and the build supports the public project prefix on navigation, data, and assets. The section-by-section revision record lists the reviewed subsections and removed instructions. The earlier coverage records below describe the imported teaching material.

Earlier section-by-section coverage record

Section-by-section context audit

This pass read all 50 lessons, including their subsections. Revisions define local inputs, domains, widths, measurement outcomes, and overloaded symbols. New drawings explain window lookup and cleanup, phase-sensitive readout, compiler decomposition, detector connectivity, carry escape, independent factory inputs, and phase estimation. Existing source circuits and relevant register tables remain available.

This is an exposition and consistency audit, not a rerun of the authors’ compiler or noise simulations. Tables remain preferable for exact mappings; a diagram is added where connectivity, branching, or operation order carries information. The register-width distinction and randomized affine exceptions in Section III were corrected.

Machine-readable review record. Checks on the revised output cover math rendering, internal links, diagram structure, and the new small algebraic examples; they are not browser pixel-layout tests.

Three kinds of evidence

EvidenceWhat these notes establish
Algebra and disclosed circuitsCheck identities, phase conventions, and finite input domains.
Compiler and decoder resultsExplain the published schedule and simulation settings.
Heuristic and hardware assumptionsState the conditions used by the end-to-end estimate.

Checks with mathematical consequences

The checks cover reversible arithmetic replay, signed gcd updates, temporary-AND and history-compression circuits, Fourier sign conventions, the linear \(2p_f\) success correction, and conditioning in distillation. The CCZ correction polynomial was checked on all 512 data/outcome assignments; all 190 Q66 representatives were checked for logical action, stabilizer commutation, and the listed parallel supports. The zero-level encoder check covers 120 single two-qubit Pauli faults.

Details that change interpretation

Source quantityHow to read it
≈39 million / 40,420,330 ToffolisDifferent counting conventions; the second is the compiled injection count.
29.50 ms per layerRounded. Appendix E23 gives 29.4958 ms, reproducing 25.690 days.
40.7% conservative branchRequires recovery search covering the omitted-window ambiguity, and modeled hardware reliability.
26.46% hardware failureCombines categories as independent. Their union bound is about 27.44%.

Appendix B writes the subtraction bound directly in combinatorial counts. The Eastin lesson distinguishes its leading \(28p^2\) term from the exact accepted-output error.

Diagrams and data

Source circuits and routing drawings remain available at full resolution, including both panels of Figure 21. Annotated equations, state traces, and support diagrams explain the smaller mechanisms. The runtime chart uses disclosed table values. Figures 7 and 22 link to the source PDF because point-by-point simulation samples are not supplied.

Scope of verification

The authors’ internal compiler and full noise simulations were not rerun. Automated checks cover generated mathematics, links, assets, and heading targets. The Fourier visual’s static fallback and both controls are checked against an exact inverse Fourier transform for all 49 settings; this is not browser pixel-layout testing. The evidence ledger records claim provenance, and Limitations collects the scientific gaps.
